text:
The Kings arrive in New Jersey on the third stop of a five-game road trip (2-0-0 so far), fresh off a 3-2 overtime win at NYI where Brandt Clarke scored the winner and Darcy Kuemper made 41 saves. They're 2-2-1 in their last five and play without Alex Turcotte, though Quinton Byfield is day-to-day and could return. The Devils are 4-1-0 over their last five after a 4-1 win over ANA, which is winless in five. This is the first meeting of the season; New Jersey won both last year.

The underlying numbers favor the home side. NJD has taken 60% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five, against 50% for LAK, and our model projects 3.23 goals for the Devils to 2.74 for the Kings. LAK also takes 4.6 penalties a game, which keeps feeding opposing power plays. In net, projected starters Kuemper (-1.2 goals saved above expected, a measure of how many goals he's stopped beyond what the shots predicted) and Jake Allen (-3.4) have both struggled this year. Last season Allen was +5.4 and Kuemper -6.8.

Jack Hughes is the Devil to watch: we give him a 35% chance to score and 71% to record a point. Nico Hischier runs the top power play. For the Kings, Artemi Panarin has a 68% point chance, and Adrian Kempe leads the group at 35% to score. Alex Laferriere plays near his hometown of Chatham.
